title: When the Postcards Sings
premise: Theo Sterling, once a celebrated piano prodigy whose career collapsed at nineteen, has spent fifteen years hiding in plain sight as a janitor at the conservatory that made and unmade her. When Mirela Vance, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, asks Theo to become her final student, Theo resists—until she realizes the language's songs are the same melodies her grandmother hummed, melodies she has spent her life refusing to hear. As Mirela's health fails, Theo must return to the recital hall where her breakdown happened, transcribing and performing the songs before they vanish with their last speaker. The novel ends with Theo teaching the recovered songs to conservatory children, no longer a tenant of her own life but its author.
about_author: Xanthe Lockridge is the pen name of a former music teacher who spent a decade documenting endangered folk songs across coastal villages before turning to fiction. Her work explores how art survives in ordinary hands.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Theo mops the conservatory floors at dawn, invisible among students who don't know she was once its most famous pupil. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: numb routine masking old shame; establishes her self-imposed exile.

chapters.title: Mirela in the Stairwell
chapters.summary: An elderly woman is found sitting on the practice-room stairs, humming an unfamiliar melody. She introduces herself as Mirela Vance and says she's been looking for someone. POV: Theo. Beat: first crack in Theo's sealed world—curiosity she immediately suppresses.

chapters.title: What the Custodian Knows
chapters.summary: Mirela returns daily, asking Theo questions about the building's acoustics, claiming certain rooms 'remember' songs. The headmaster warns Theo to keep the eccentric visitor away. POV: Theo. Beat: quiet defiance stirring; Theo begins listening despite herself.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Humming
chapters.summary: Mirela sings a lullaby and Theo freezes—it's the melody her grandmother hummed while cooking, a song Theo never learned the words to. POV: Theo, with flashback. Beat: recognition and grief collide; the past becomes urgent.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Mirela reveals she is the last speaker of her language and asks Theo to be her final student. Theo refuses, citing her hands, her history, her fear. POV: Theo. Beat: refusal born of terror, not indifference—the central wound named.

chapters.title: Nineteen
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the disastrous debut recital where seventeen-year-old Theo froze mid-concerto, her mentor's cruelty echoing in the silence. POV: Theo (past). Beat: the reader finally sees the story that went wrong; sympathy deepens.

chapters.title: A Reason to Say Yes
chapters.summary: Theo finds Mirela collapsed outside the conservatory gate. In the hospital, Mirela admits time is short. Theo agrees—not to perform, only to learn and transcribe. POV: Theo. Beat: reluctant commitment; a door opens a crack.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Kitchen
chapters.summary: First lessons in Mirela's cramped apartment: words without writing, songs carried in breath. Theo struggles; her trained ear fights the oral tradition. POV: Theo. Beat: humility; unlearning begins, frustrating and liberating.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: The headmaster discovers Theo's visits and threatens her job, invoking her 'unreliability.' Theo nearly quits the lessons. POV: Theo, brief interlude from Mirela. Beat: external pressure rises; stakes become material.

chapters.title: Songs in the Walls
chapters.summary: Mirela explains her people once sang in this city's markets before being scattered; the conservatory itself was built over their gathering hall. POV: Mirela. Beat: the personal story widens into inheritance and erasure; Theo sees her janitor's mop as an instrument of that erasure.

chapters.title: Transcription Nights
chapters.summary: Theo secretly notates the songs at night in the empty recital hall, testing them on the piano. The notes fit—and transform. POV: Theo. Beat: cautious joy; craft reawakening, but performance still unthinkable.

chapters.title: The Rival Memory
chapters.summary: A young ethnomusicologist, Dev Anand, arrives hunting Mirela's recordings for an archive, offering money and 'preservation.' Mirela distrusts him; Theo feels threatened by his credentials. POV: alternating. Beat: competition and doubt—who owns a dying song?

chapters.title: Broken Verse
chapters.summary: Mirela's memory falters mid-lesson; a song loses its ending. Panic sets in—there may be no second chances. Theo records obsessively. POV: Theo. Beat: ticking clock accelerates; grief anticipates loss.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Sent
chapters.summary: Cleaning the archives, Theo finds a letter her mentor wrote decades ago admitting his own stolen teachers—a lineage of theft and debt. POV: Theo. Beat: her villain humanized; anger complicated into understanding.

chapters.title: Dev's Offer
chapters.summary: Dev offers Theo co-authorship on the archive project if she surrenders her transcriptions. Tempted by legitimacy, she almost signs. POV: Theo. Beat: the seduction of respectability versus ownership of her own voice.

chapters.title: Mirela's Verdict
chapters.summary: Mirela learns of the offer and, furious, tells Theo she isn't a student but still a servant of other people's approval. POV: Mirela, then Theo alone all night. Beat: lowest point; the relationship fractures.

chapters.title: Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Weeks pass. Theo cleans rooms she no longer hears, the transcriptions locked in a drawer. Mirela is hospitalized again. POV: Theo. Beat: desolation; everything gained now at risk of total loss.

chapters.title: The Recital Hall at Midnight
chapters.summary: Theo breaks into the recital hall where she failed at nineteen and plays the recovered songs alone until dawn—grief, apology, and finally power in her hands. POV: Theo. Beat: cathartic turning point; she chooses the hall instead of fleeing it.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in Ward Six
chapters.summary: Theo brings the finished transcription to Mirela's hospital bed and sings the broken verse's ending back to her—from memory. Mirela weeps and forgives. POV: alternating. Beat: repair; the student becomes keeper.

chapters.title: One Night Only
chapters.summary: Mirela's dying wish: one public singing in the recital hall. Theo organizes it against the headmaster's objections; students, Dev, and strangers fill the seats. POV: Theo. Beat: rising climax; terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker Sings
chapters.summary: In the hall where Theo broke, Mirela sings the full cycle with Theo accompanying, then teaches the audience the chorus so hundreds of voices carry it forward. Mirela dies peacefully days later. POV: Theo. Beat: climax and release; the language outlives its last speaker.

chapters.title: Authorship
chapters.summary: Theo resigns from custodial work—or rather, reframes it—and begins a children's song class at the conservatory, her name on the door at last. She hums her grandmother's lullaby with the words. POV: Theo. Beat: resolution; inheritance accepted, identity claimed, the song continued.
